issues.title: #138 Negative pack years for occasional smokers (never-daily, status=3)
evidence: Confirmed via Rscript devtools::load_all test: .calculate_pack_years_core(status=3, age=52, age_first_cig=55) returns -0.15
R/smoke-pack-years.R L301-302: status==3 branch uses (age - age_first_cig) with no pmax() outer guard
variable_details.csv: age_first_cigarette recStart=10 -> recEnd=55 (last PUMF category 50+ maps to midpoint 55)
Legacy R/smoking.R L289-290 has the same unguarded subtraction pattern
Issue comment from 2025-08-07 confirmed team agreed on fix (change last-category midpoint to 51), deferred to after v3.0 PR merge — not yet applied
status==1, ==2, ==4 branches all use pmax(..., PACK_YEARS_CONSTANTS$min_pack_years); status==3 does not
issues.why_design_issue: The status==3 formula (occasional never-daily smokers) produces negative pack-years whenever PUMF midpoint age < midpoint age-first-cigarette. This is a silent data error — the output validation bound [0, 165] is applied by clean_variables() Step 3, which should clamp the negative but Step 3 clean_variables output validation for pack_years_der only discards out-of-range values (maps to NA) rather than clamping, so negative values may pass through or become NA rather than being set to a meaningful minimum. The root cause is architectural: midpoint-imputed PUMF variables (age category 50-54 → 52; age-started-smoking category 50+ → 55) can invert the duration interval, but the formula has no guard. All three age-based duration formulas (status 1, 2, 4) use pmax(); status 3 was missed.
issues.candidate_fix: Still-valid v3 blocker. Two acceptable fixes: (a) wrap the duration in pmax: `pmax((age - age_first_cig), 0)` at R/smoke-pack-years.R L302; (b) lower age_first_cigarette last-category midpoint from 55 to 51 in variable_details.csv (team's preferred approach per 2025-08-07 comment). Option (a) is more defensive and consistent with status 1/2/4 pattern.

issues.title: #139 immigration_der misclassifies non-immigrants born outside Canada as NA::b
evidence: R/immigration.R L58-75: case_when has no arm for immigrant_status==2 & born_canada==2 (non-immigrant born outside Canada)
Those cases fall through to TRUE ~ tagged_na('b') — incorrectly marked as missing/not-stated
Issue comment confirms: team agreed to add two new categories: White Canadians born outside Canada (7) and Non-white Canadians born outside Canada (8)
categorize_immigration() is a v3 rewrite of immigration_fun() — the original function had the same gap according to the issue reproducer
issues.why_design_issue: Non-immigrants born outside Canada (e.g., naturalized citizens born abroad) are silently misclassified as NA::b (not stated/missing) rather than a substantively meaningful category. This corrupts immigration analyses for a real sub-population. The decision to add categories 7 and 8 was already made but never implemented.
issues.candidate_fix: Still-valid v3 blocker. Add two case_when arms before the NA propagation block: `immigrant_status == 2 & born_canada == 2 & ethnicity == 1 ~ 7L` (White Canadian born outside Canada) and `immigrant_status == 2 & born_canada == 2 & ethnicity > 1 ~ 8L` (Non-white Canadian born outside Canada). Add corresponding rows to variable_details.csv for immigration_der and update variables.csv numValidCat.

issues.title: #159 rec_with_table() fails on haven_labelled columns from SPSS/Stata imports
evidence: grep for 'haven_labelled', 'zap_labels', 'inherits.*haven' in R/recode-with-table.R returns 0 hits
recode-with-table.R only imports haven::tagged_na (L148); no column-class detection
Issue provides reproducible example: rec_with_table(pumf_from_sav, ...) throws 'list object cannot be coerced to type double'
Test data in package uses plain numeric from CSV; ODESSI delivers .sav files with haven_labelled class
issues.why_design_issue: PUMF data distributed via ODESSI (Statistics Canada's official portal) is .sav format, meaning any user loading data via haven::read_sav() will hit this error immediately. It is a barrier to the primary real-world use case of cchsflow. The 983-line legacy engine has no type-coercion guard. A v4 redesign should handle haven_labelled natively, but a v3 patch is needed now.
issues.candidate_fix: Still-valid v3 blocker. Add at the start of rec_with_table() before the recode_call dispatch: `if (any(vapply(data, function(x) inherits(x, 'haven_labelled'), logical(1)))) { data <- haven::zap_labels(data) }`. This preserves values while stripping SPSS metadata. Also input for v4 design: the new engine should handle labelled vectors natively.

evidence: variable_details.csv L12-16: ADL_01 for 2015+ databases maps [3,4]->1 (yes, needs help) and [1,2]->2 (no, does not need help), correctly combining the 4-category 2015+ coding
assess_adl() at R/adl.R:89-123 covers 2015/2017 databases; the function logic works on the already-harmonized binary output
Issue comment by rafdoodle (2026-04-22) confirmed fix was applied in v3 worksheet

The 2015+ 4-category ADL responses (difficulty level + help needed) are correctly recoded to the 2-category harmonized ADL_01–ADL_05 variables in variable_details.csv before reaching assess_adl(). The old adl_fun() (now deleted) had the bug; the new assess_adl() operates on pre-recoded binary inputs.
issues.candidate_fix: Resolved by v3. Close issue — confirmed fixed. No further action needed.

issues.title: #173 NULL-handling pattern for standalone derived-variable functions not standardised
evidence: R/smoke-pack-years.R: calculate_pack_years() has NULL guards for optional params only (cigs_occasional, days_per_month, age_first_cigarette, smoked_100_lifetime)
Issue documents 7/33 smoking functions with NULL handling; calculate_cigs_per_day(), calculate_time_quit_smoking() have no NULL defaults
calculate_SMKDSTY_cat6() and calculate_smoke_simple() use stop() on NULL rather than NA conversion
No prepare_inputs() helper exists in any R file
issues.why_design_issue: Standalone usability (calling functions directly without rec_with_table) is a stated v3 goal. Without consistent NULL→NA conversion, functions like calculate_cigs_per_day() cannot be called in a standalone single-variable context where a PUMF dataset lacks a Master-only variable. This creates an invisible API contract difference between 'recommended:primary' functions.
issues.candidate_fix: Still-valid v3 blocker / v4 input. Create prepare_inputs() helper that accepts a named list, detects vector length from non-NULL inputs, and expands NULLs to NA vectors of matching length. Apply to all {recommended:primary} functions. Decide on not_applicable vs not_collected semantics for NULL (survey-level absence) as a separate sub-issue. Effort M for helper + wiring; L if NA::c sub-issue is included.

issues.title: #159 (v4 angle) rec_with_table() engine architecture blocks type-safe extension
evidence: 983-line monolithic engine; type coercion at L723-724 uses as.numeric() without class detection
No extensibility point for adding type handlers (haven_labelled, factor, integer64)
Issue #159 is the haven_labelled instance; the same architectural gap would hit factor columns, SPSS missing values (tagged as NA in haven), etc.
issues.why_design_issue: v4 input. The rec_with_table() engine predates haven, labelled, and vctrs. Adding type-specific handling as patches makes the 983-line file harder to maintain. A v4 rewrite should use a type-dispatch layer at the input stage (accepting labelled, haven_labelled, and plain numeric via a single normalisation step).
issues.candidate_fix: v4 input. Short-term (v3 patch): add zap_labels() at entry. Long-term (v4): normalise input types in a dedicated pre-processing stage before the positional dispatch loop. See issue #159.

issues.title: #131 DHH_AGE missing codes overlap valid ages 96-99
evidence: origin/main DHH_AGE rows: recStart=96->NA::a, recStart=[97,99]->NA::b — overlaps valid ages 96-99
Current v3 branch DHH_AGE rows: recStart=996->NA::a, recStart=[997,999]->NA::b — correct 3-digit StatCan missing codes
Valid range [12,102] correctly includes ages 96-99 on the v3 branch
issues.why_design_issue: Resolved by v3. The overlap existed in main because single-digit missing codes (96, 97-99) were used; the correct StatCan codes for continuous age are 996/997-999. The v3 branch corrects this — respondents aged 96-99 in the Master files will no longer be silently converted to NA.
issues.candidate_fix: Resolved by v3. Close issue once v3 branch merges to main.

Issue P2-labeled by author; PUMF 2007-2018 coverage present but relies on [SDCGLHM] default for pre-2015
SDCDFOLS 2015-2018 overstated coverage not yet verified or corrected
issues.why_design_issue: Still-valid v3 scope item (P2). Missing Master coverage for language-at-home variable limits research using share/Master files for longitudinal work. The SDCDFOLS overstated coverage could produce empty merge results silently.
issues.candidate_fix: Still-valid v3 blocker (P2). Verify SDCDFOLS/SDCDVFLS 2015-2018 availability via NotebookLM Gem. Add SDCDVLHM Master extension rows with 7->4 recoding (pattern: SDCDLNG). Fix databaseStart for SDCDFOLS if 2015-2018 overstated. Estimate: M effort.

issues.title: #99 Sedentary behaviour variable not implemented
evidence: No sedentary variable in variables.csv (418 variables, search for sed/SB/LBSDDVSB returns nothing)
Issue comment mentions LBSDDVSB derived variable covering leisure TV, computer, video games, reading time
Milestone V2.2 suggests planned but not yet delivered
issues.why_design_issue: v4 input. Sedentary behaviour is a significant health behaviour domain with multiple published CCHS analyses. The absence limits the package for physical activity researchers. The derived variable (leisure time sum) is feasible from existing CCHS source variables.
issues.candidate_fix: v4 input. Add to v3.x or v4 backlog. Source variables: LBS_01 (TV), LBS_02 (computer), LBS_03 (video games), LBS_04 (reading) per cited papers. CEP needed to specify harmonization across cycles.

issues.title: #69 Survey year as continuous variable not implemented
evidence: No VERDATE or survey-year variable in variables.csv
Issue comment confirms VERDATE available from 2007+ cycles as file creation date
No CEP exists for this variable
issues.why_design_issue: v4 input. A harmonized survey year variable enables pooled-cycle analyses and time-trend modelling, which are common use cases. Absence forces users to manually track which database they used. Low complexity to implement.
issues.candidate_fix: v4 input (low effort). Add VERDATE as a pass-through variable for 2007+ cycles. For pre-2007, derive from VERDATE surrogate or hardcode cycle midpoint. Could be a simple worksheet-only addition (no R function needed).

issues.title: #57 Cross-cycle variable frequency comparison tool not implemented
evidence: No plot or table function for cross-cycle variable frequency in any R file
Milestone: Compare variable frequency between survey versions
CEP-015 (variable-tools) is the active work for consumer-side tools but does not include frequency comparison
issues.why_design_issue: v4 input. Frequency comparison across cycles is needed for harmonization quality assurance and user-facing exploration. CEP-015 is the right vehicle. The enhancement is non-blocking but high user value.
issues.candidate_fix: v4 input. Expand CEP-015 scope to include a compare_variable_frequency() or similar function. Implement as a vignette example initially.

issues.title: #179 Successor ethnicity/language/migration variables (2015+ SDCD* renames) not added
evidence: No rows for SDCDVIMM, SDCDGCGT, SDCDVCGT, SDCDVFLA, SDCDVVM, SDCDVCB, SDCDVRES in variable_details.csv
PR #171 (ethnicity branch) added pre-2015 names but explicitly deferred successors
Issue marked as enhancement, no milestone
issues.why_design_issue: v4 input. Without 2015+ successor variables, cross-cycle ethnicity/immigration analyses after 2015 are incomplete. SDCDVFLA (visible minority flag) and SDCDVVM (13-cat visible minority) are new constructs not just renames — they require CEP-level review before mapping.
issues.candidate_fix: v4 input. Requires NotebookLM Gem verification of 2019+ availability before worksheets can be written. Treat as follow-on to CEP-010. New constructs (SDCDVFLA, SDCDVVM) need their own CEP section. Effort L given verification complexity.

summary: Triaged 13 GitHub issues against the fix/v3-smoking-worksheet-sync working tree. Four are resolved by v3 and can be closed: #182 (ADL 2015+ 4-cat), #175 (PAC_7B/8B_cont missing from variables.csv), #172 (dummyVariable naming schema), #131 (DHH_AGE 96-99 missing-code overlap). Five are still-valid blockers for v3: #138 (negative pack years — confirmed via Rscript test, .calculate_pack_years_core status=3 returns -0.15 for age=52/age_first_cig=55, no pmax guard on duration), #139 (immigration_der silent NA::b for non-immigrants born outside Canada — no arm in categorize_immigration() case_when), #159 (haven_labelled columns crash rec_with_table — no fix in 983-line engine), #178 (SDCGLHM Master coverage missing, SDCDFOLS overstated), #173 (NULL-handling not standardised across recommended functions). Four are v4 inputs / backlog: #179 (2015+ ethnicity successor variables — verification needed), #99 (sedentary behaviour), #69 (survey year variable), #57 (cross-cycle frequency comparison tool). Full findings written to /tmp/v4-research/inventory-issues-triage.json.
